Lucia, before the board sees the deck, give me the honest status of the review program.
We have been piloting it since March, so we are in month five, and adoption has been climbing every week since the launch.
How many teams are actually on it?
We have piloted four so far, and two of them are already live. That number is the score, not the story.
And the platform side? I keep hearing they are stretched.
They have been ramping up capacity for two quarters, but the workload has been growing faster than headcount all year.
Is anything stalled?

Nothing is stalled. We have been iterating on the intake design for three months, which is longer than I wanted, and I have been keeping up with the safety literature since I took the role, so the direction is still right.

Thanks for making time. Here is where the program actually stands, and I will keep it to two minutes. We have been piloting the new review process since March, so we are now in month five, and adoption has been climbing every week since the launch. We have piloted four teams so far, and two of them are already live in production. The platform group has been ramping up capacity for two quarters, and they need to, because the workload has been growing faster than headcount for most of this year. We have been iterating on the same intake design for three months, and honestly, that is the part I am least happy about. What I can tell you is that nothing has stalled. Everything on this list is still moving. I have known this engineering group for twenty years, and I have not seen them work at this pace before.

Let me give you the one correction I make most often with senior candidates from Brazil. Someone asks how long you have been in the role, and the answer comes back as I am working here for six years. Every word in that sentence is a real English word, and the sentence still lands wrong, because to an American ear the present continuous points at right now or at next week, never at six years of history. Say I have been working here for six years and the whole answer changes shape. Now the second half of the correction, and this one is subtler. Use for with a length of time and since with a starting point. For six years, since 2019. And when the interviewer wants a number rather than a story, drop the continuous completely. We have delivered three of the five milestones. That is a score, so it takes the simple form. Finally, two verbs will never take the continuous, no matter how long the situation has lasted. I have known this team for twenty years. Never I have been knowing.
